name: 01_basics_callback_flow.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Basics Callback Flow
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Start here: learn when OnInitialize, OnPreLayout, and OnLayout run, and
why every frame must be calculated directly from ctx.time.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Correct: closed-form function of ctx.time, safe to evaluate for any
    -- frame in any order.
    ctx.global.rotation = ctx.time * 20.0

    -- Wrong (left commented out on purpose): this looks like "advance by 1
    -- degree per frame", but ctx.global.rotation is rebuilt from the host
    -- inspector value on every call, so it never accumulates.
    -- ctx.global.rotation = ctx.global.rotation + 1.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- ctx.global.rotation here is the CONFIRMED value from OnPreLayout
    -- above (read-only at this point), not the raw inspector value.
    -- print("confirmed global rotation =", ctx.global.rotation)

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        -- Also a pure function of (ctx.time, index): scrubbing backward or
        -- rendering frames out of order reproduces the exact same motion.
        character.rotation = math.sin(ctx.time * 2.0 + index * 0.2) * 15.0
    end
end
description:
Start here: learn when OnInitialize, OnPreLayout, and OnLayout run, and
why every frame must be calculated directly from ctx.time.
title: Basics Callback Flow
author: Mug

name: 02_shared_state.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Shared State
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.1
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Compute constants once at chunk scope and read them from every callback, the
replacement for the deprecated mt.storage table.
]]

-- The Lua state lives for as long as the script does, not for a single frame, so a local declared
-- here is still there on the next callback and the next frame. Build anything expensive once, up
-- here, and the callbacks only read it.
--
-- This replaces mt.storage, which is deprecated. Storage froze its contents after OnInitialize so
-- later callbacks could not corrupt them, but keeping your own values intact is easier to reason
-- about than a second lifetime with its own rules. Storage also only accepted booleans, numbers,
-- strings and tables, so anything else -- an mt.svg_path template, for one -- could never live
-- there anyway.
local amplitude = 0.06
local swayDegrees = 4.0

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Prefer instance_seed + mt.random*: closed-form, survives text growth, and
    -- differs across instances of the same script (a fixed literal seed would
    -- repeat the same pattern on every instance).
    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local phase = mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(ctx.time * 2.0 + phase) * amplitude
        character.rotation = math.sin(ctx.time * 1.5 + phase) * swayDegrees
    end
end
description:
Compute constants once at chunk scope and read them from every callback, the
replacement for the deprecated mt.storage table.
title: Shared State
author: Mug

name: 03_mt_timeline.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 3
-- @title MT Timeline
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Choose clip-relative progress for whole-span motion, or real seconds for
fixed-speed intros and outros. Demonstrates all current mt.timeline helpers.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- ctx.timeline fields, all clip-local (clip start is always frame/time 0).
    -- print("available", ctx.timeline.available)
    -- print("start_frame/end_frame", ctx.timeline.start_frame, ctx.timeline.end_frame)
    -- print("duration_seconds", ctx.timeline.duration_seconds)
    -- print("progress (0..1)", ctx.timeline.progress)

    -- available is false when the host cannot resolve a finite clip range
    -- (for example scripting in isolation); the other fields fall back to 0
    -- in that case, so always guard clip-length-dependent logic with it.

    -- Whole-span motion (drift across the ENTIRE clip): this is the one
    -- case where clip-relative progress is correct, since the drift should
    -- take longer if the clip is longer. Base values (ctx.global) can only
    -- be written here, in OnPreLayout.
    local sweepProgress = mt.timeline.progress(ctx)
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5 + (sweepProgress - 0.5) * 0.1
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Resolve the host clip length, or use 4 seconds when it is unavailable.
    local clipDuration = mt.timeline.duration(ctx)

    -- WRONG for a fixed-speed reveal: typing speed changes with clip length.
    -- local visible = math.floor(mt.timeline.progress(ctx) * ctx.char_count)

    -- RIGHT: constant 0.12s per character regardless of clip length.
    local secondsPerCharacter = 0.12
    local visibleCount = math.floor(ctx.time / secondsPerCharacter)

    -- Intro anchored to clip start, outro anchored to clip end, both at a
    -- fixed real-time speed (auto-compressed only if the clip is shorter
    -- than introSeconds + outroSeconds). ctx.global is read-only by this
    -- point, so the fade is applied per-character instead.
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, 0.6, 0.6)
    local introOutroFade = mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroProgress))

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        character.opacity = introOutroFade
        if index > visibleCount then
            character.opacity = 0.0
        end
    end

    -- Outro fade over the last 0.4s of the clip, anchored to the clip end --
    -- built from mt.timeline.remaining directly, for cases that need only
    -- the outro half.
    local outroFade = mt.clamp(mt.timeline.remaining(ctx) / 0.4, 0.0, 1.0)
    -- ctx.chars[1].scale = 1.0 - (1.0 - outroFade) * 0.2
    -- print("resolved duration", clipDuration)
end
description:
Choose clip-relative progress for whole-span motion, or real seconds for
fixed-speed intros and outros. Demonstrates all current mt.timeline helpers.
title: MT Timeline
author: Mug

name: 04_global.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Global
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Use ctx.global in OnPreLayout to control the whole text block. Transform,
fill, gradient, stroke, and shadow are grouped for easy experimentation.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Transform: position is 0..1 canvas fraction, rotation/yaw/pitch in
    -- degrees, pivot is the point transforms are applied around.
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 0.05
    ctx.global.position_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 10.0
    -- ctx.global.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 15.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- ctx.global.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.13) * 10.0 -- 3D preset only
    ctx.global.scale = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25) * 0.1
    ctx.global.stretch_x = 1.0
    ctx.global.stretch_y = 1.0
    ctx.global.pivot_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_y = 0.5
    -- Opacity multiplies with the character and part opacity below and
    -- applies to fill, gradient, stroke, shadow, and the bounding box alike.
    ctx.global.opacity = 0.5 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.15)) * 0.5

    -- Fill color and optional gradient overlay; the gradient angle spins.
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    -- ctx.global.fill.transparent = true -- keep stroke/shadow, hide fill
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab" -- "none" disables the gradient
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = { r = 0.2, g = 0.6, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.gradient.midpoint = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.3
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = ctx.time * 30.0
    ctx.global.gradient.start_position = 0.0
    ctx.global.gradient.end_position = 1.0

    -- Stroke outline, pulsing width.
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.01 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.02
    ctx.global.stroke.gap = 0.0
    ctx.global.stroke.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "stroke_over_fill" -- or "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.stroke.miter_limit = 4.0

    -- Drop shadow, sweeping angle.
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.5 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2)) * 2.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = ctx.time * 60.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.5 }
end
description:
Use ctx.global in OnPreLayout to control the whole text block. Transform,
fill, gradient, stroke, and shadow are grouped for easy experimentation.
title: Global
author: Mug

name: 05_camera.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Camera
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Control the 3D camera from OnPreLayout. Enable 3D Projection to compare
target, yaw, pitch, perspective, zoom, and lens shift.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Target: the point the camera looks at, in host-normalized
    -- coordinates. Y grows upward.
    ctx.camera.target_x = 0.5
    ctx.camera.target_y = 0.5

    -- Orbit angles in degrees, sweeping back and forth.
    ctx.camera.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 25.0
    ctx.camera.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.07, math.pi / 2.0) * 12.0

    -- Perspective strength: higher values exaggerate depth.
    ctx.camera.perspective = 0.55 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.08) * 0.25

    -- Zoom multiplier: higher values move the camera closer.
    ctx.camera.zoom = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.12) * 0.1

    -- Lens shift: principal-point offset as a canvas fraction, independent
    -- of the orbit angles. Y grows upward.
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_x = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.06) * 0.03
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_y = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.09, math.pi / 2.0) * 0.02
end
description:
Control the 3D camera from OnPreLayout. Enable 3D Projection to compare
target, yaw, pitch, perspective, zoom, and lens shift.
title: Camera
author: Mug

name: 06_character.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Character
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Read and modify individual characters through ctx.chars in OnLayout.
The second character is isolated so each transform and style is easy to see.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 2 then
        return
    end

    local character = ctx.chars[2]

    -- Read-only identity and geometry.
    -- print(character.index, character.text, character.line_index)
    -- print(character.geometry.bounds_center_x, character.geometry.bounds_center_y)

    -- Transform: offset is 0.5-centered (0.5 = no displacement), pivot is
    -- the point rotation/scale are applied around, in host-normalized
    -- coordinates. Y grows upward.
    character.offset_x = 0.5
    character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.5) * 0.08
    character.pivot_x = 0.5
    character.pivot_y = 0.5
    character.scale = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.4) * 0.3
    character.stretch_x = 1.0
    character.stretch_y = 1.0
    character.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3) * 20.0
    -- character.z = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.3 -- 3D preset only
    -- character.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 20.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- character.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25) * 10.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- Opacity multiplies with ctx.global.opacity and the owning parts' opacity.
    character.opacity = 0.4 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.6)) * 0.6

    -- Per-character fill overrides the global fill only while fill.use
    -- is true; hue cycles over time.
    character.fill.use = true
    character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0), 0.8, 1.0, 1.0)

    -- Per-character stroke overrides the global stroke width/gap/color
    -- only while stroke.use is true.
    -- character.stroke.use = true
    -- character.stroke.width = 0.01 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.02
    -- character.stroke.gap = 0.0
    -- character.stroke.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }

    -- Per-character shadow color overrides the global shadow color only
    -- while shadow.use is true.
    -- character.shadow.use = true
    -- character.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.3, a = 0.6 }
end
description:
Read and modify individual characters through ctx.chars in OnLayout.
The second character is isolated so each transform and style is easy to see.
title: Character
author: Mug

name: 07_part.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "%=%"
-- @title Part
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Filter and style glyph parts with mt.each_part. The recommended text makes
character ownership, per-character indices, and continuous progress easy to compare.
]]

local kWindowSize = 2
local kWindowPeriod = 2.5

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local maximumWindowStart = math.max(ctx.char_count - kWindowSize + 1, 1)
    local windowStart =
        math.floor(mt.cycle(ctx.time, kWindowPeriod) * maximumWindowStart) + 1
    local windowEnd = math.min(windowStart + kWindowSize - 1, ctx.char_count)

    -- Filter by owning character. info.progress remains continuous across the
    -- filtered set instead of restarting at each character boundary.
    for index, part, info in mt.each_part(ctx, {
        from_char = windowStart,
        to_char = windowEnd,
    }) do
        local phase = info.index_in_char * 0.8 + info.char_index * 0.3
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.5, phase) * 0.04
        part.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.35, phase) * 12.0

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(
            mt.wrap(info.progress * 0.8 + ctx.time * 0.05, 0.0, 1.0),
            0.7,
            1.0
        )

        -- info.char directly exposes the owning character.
        local belongsToOwner =
            index >= info.char.part_start
            and index < info.char.part_start + info.char.part_count
        assert(belongsToOwner, "part ownership range is inconsistent")
    end
end
description:
Filter and style glyph parts with mt.each_part. The recommended text makes
character ownership, per-character indices, and continuous progress easy to compare.
title: Part
author: Mug

name: 08_inheritance.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- @title Inheritance
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
See style inheritance from global to character to part. Toggle each `use`
flag to compare inherited and explicitly overridden values.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Global fill is white, but the gradient overlay repaints anything that
    -- is not using an individual color.
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab"
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = { r = 0.2, g = 0.6, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Character 1: fill.use toggles on a slow square wave. While it is
    -- false, this character is painted by the gradient like the rest of
    -- the untouched text; the instant it flips to true, a flat red wins
    -- over the gradient entirely.
    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[1]
        character.fill.use = mt.wave_square(ctx.time, 0.2) > 0.0
        character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.2, b = 0.2, a = 1.0 }
    end

    -- Character 2: fill.use stays true throughout, but the flat color
    -- itself cycles hue -- contrast this with character 1's on/off flip.
    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        local character = ctx.chars[2]
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0), 0.8, 1.0)
    end

    -- Character 3, part 1: the character's OWN fill.use stays false
    -- (inherits Global/gradient throughout), but the first owned part
    -- toggles fill.use on its own square wave -- out of phase with
    -- character 1 -- so only that one part ever differs from its
    -- character, and only while its own toggle is on.
    if ctx.char_count >= 3 and ctx.part_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[3]
        if character.part_count >= 1 then
            local part = ctx.parts[character.part_start]
            part.fill.use = mt.wave_square(ctx.time, 0.2, math.pi) > 0.0
            part.fill.color = { r = 0.2, g = 1.0, b = 0.4, a = 1.0 }
        end
    end

    -- Shadow color follows the exact same chain as fill: a character's
    -- resolved shadow.color propagates down to its owned parts unless a
    -- part sets shadow.use = true itself.
    -- ctx.chars[1].shadow.use = true
    -- ctx.chars[1].shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.6 }
end
description:
See style inheritance from global to character to part. Toggle each `use`
flag to compare inherited and explicitly overridden values.
title: Inheritance
author: Mug

name: 09_bounding_box.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Bounding Box
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Draw and animate the text frame through ctx.bounding_box in OnLayout.
This is independent from the write-on and draw-order controls in ctx.output.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- The box outline itself, all 4 edges drawn with rounded caps.
    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = true
    ctx.bounding_box.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.start_cap = "round" -- see MtBoundingBox for valid caps
    ctx.bounding_box.end_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.corner_radius = 1.0

    -- Outline width pulses so the stroke's own animation is unambiguous.
    ctx.bounding_box.width = 3.0 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25)) * 6.0

    -- Margin between the text and the box breathes in and out, so the box
    -- itself visibly grows/shrinks around the (otherwise static) text.
    local margin = 2.0 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2)) * 8.0
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = margin
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = margin

    -- Fill behind the text, independent of the outline; opacity cycles.
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = 0.15 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.3

    -- Fill and stroke can be nudged independently of each other and of the
    -- text/margin above (for a detached-shadow-like offset look).
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_offset_x = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_offset_y = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_x = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_y = 0.0
end
description:
Draw and animate the text frame through ctx.bounding_box in OnLayout.
This is independent from the write-on and draw-order controls in ctx.output.
title: Bounding Box
author: Mug

name: 10_output.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Output
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Use ctx.output in OnLayout for write-on animation, filtering, and draw order.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Write-on reveal range, normalized 0.0..1.0 across the whole sequence.
    -- write_on_mode selects whether that range advances through characters
    -- or parts. Here the reveal sweeps forward and back on a 4-second
    -- cycle, so characters visibly appear and disappear in text order.
    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "character" -- or "part"
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 4.0)

    -- Manual reveal and draw order overrides the natural text order; see
    -- MtOutput for the manual_order_text syntax. Uncomment to reveal
    -- characters 3, then 1, then 2 instead of left-to-right.
    -- ctx.output.manual_order_enabled = true
    -- ctx.output.manual_order_text = "3,1,2"

    -- reorder_parts affects only multi-part characters (for example CJK
    -- strokes or symbols like "%"/"="), so it has no visible effect on
    -- plain single-part Latin text.
    -- ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
end
description: Use ctx.output in OnLayout for write-on animation, filtering, and draw order.
title: Output
author: Mug

name: 11_layout_shaping.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- @title Layout Shaping
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Change text shaping before layout: text, tracking, line spacing, writing
direction, alignment, and per-character margins.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Text and font can be reassigned; font_name must be one of ctx.fonts.
    ctx.global.text = "Line one\nLine two\nLine three"
    -- ctx.global.font_name = ctx.fonts[1]

    -- Extra spacing added between characters, breathing in and out.
    ctx.global.tracking = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.06

    -- Multiplies the distance between lines.
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.15) * 0.4

    -- Switches to vertical (top-to-bottom) writing.
    -- ctx.global.vertical = true

    -- Horizontal alignment: "left" | "center" | "right". Cycled on a
    -- 3-second step so each value is visibly held, not blended.
    local horizontalAlignments = { "left", "center", "right" }
    local horizontalStep = math.floor(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0) * #horizontalAlignments) + 1
    ctx.global.h_align = horizontalAlignments[horizontalStep]

    -- Vertical alignment: "top" | "center" | "bottom" | "baseline". Cycled
    -- independently on its own 4-second step.
    local verticalAlignments = { "top", "center", "bottom", "baseline" }
    local verticalStep = math.floor(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 4.0) * #verticalAlignments) + 1
    ctx.global.v_align = verticalAlignments[verticalStep]

    -- Per-character extra margin, indexed from 1. Missing indices default
    -- to zero, so a short table only affects the first characters. Here
    -- the margin before the second character pulses over time.
    ctx.global.margins = { 0.0, mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.12 }
end
description:
Change text shaping before layout: text, tracking, line spacing, writing
direction, alignment, and per-character margins.
title: Layout Shaping
author: Mug

name: 12_mt_color.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title MT Color
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Resolve inherited fills, then create, fade, and interpolate colors with
mt.color without changing the input colors.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- from_hsv builds an RGBA color from normalized hue/saturation/value.
    local hueColor = mt.color.from_hsv(0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0)

    -- from_oklch builds an RGBA color from the perceptually-uniform OKLCH
    -- space (lightness, chroma, hue); useful when interpolating hues needs
    -- to look perceptually even, unlike raw HSV interpolation.
    local oklchColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.75, 0.15, 0.6, 1.0)

    -- lerp interpolates two RGBA color tables component-wise.
    local red = { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    local blue = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    local mixed = mt.color.lerp(red, blue, 0.5)

    -- with_alpha copies a color while replacing only its alpha channel.
    local translucentRed = mt.color.with_alpha(red, 0.4)

    for _, character, info in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        -- Resolve the color, fill mode, and combined object opacity currently
        -- inherited by this character before replacing it with a solid color.
        local inheritedColor, fillMode, resolvedOpacity =
            mt.color.resolve_fill(ctx, character)
        local hue = info.progress
        if resolvedOpacity > 0.0 then
            local hueColor = mt.color.from_hsv(hue, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0)
            local mixAmount = fillMode == "solid" and 0.55 or 0.8
            character.fill.use = true
            character.fill.color =
                mt.color.lerp(inheritedColor, hueColor, mixAmount)
        end
    end

    -- Uncomment to inspect the constructed colors directly.
    -- print(hueColor.r, hueColor.g, hueColor.b, hueColor.a)
    -- print(oklchColor.r, oklchColor.g, oklchColor.b)
    -- print(mixed.r, mixed.g, mixed.b)
    -- print(translucentRed.a)
end
description:
Resolve inherited fills, then create, fade, and interpolate colors with

name: 13_mt_values.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "VALUES"
-- @title MT Values
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Normalize, remap, interpolate, and repeat values with the core mt helpers.
Each result drives a visible character property.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local progress = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 2.0)
    local eased = mt.smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, progress)

    for _, character, info in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local position = info.progress

        -- remap converts the 0..1 character position into a canvas offset;
        -- inverse_lerp converts that result back to normalized progress.
        local horizontal = mt.remap(position, 0.0, 1.0, -0.08, 0.08, true)
        local recovered = mt.inverse_lerp(-0.08, 0.08, horizontal)
        character.offset_x = 0.5 + horizontal
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.lerp(-0.06, 0.06, eased)
        character.scale = 0.8 + mt.saturate(recovered) * 0.4

        -- lerp_angle takes the short route across the 0/360-degree seam.
        character.rotation = mt.lerp_angle(350.0, 10.0, progress)
        character.opacity = mt.clamp(0.35 + eased, 0.0, 1.0)

        -- cycle repeats in 0..1; wrap keeps the added hue in the same range.
        local hue = mt.wrap(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0) + position, 0.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(hue, 0.7, 1.0)
    end
end
description:
Normalize, remap, interpolate, and repeat values with the core mt helpers.
Each result drives a visible character property.
title: MT Values
author: Mug

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- @title MT Stagger
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Create per-character delays with mt.stagger, then compare ascending, descending,
center-out, and random ordering with mt.stagger_pattern.
]]

local kDelay = 0.08
local kDuration = 0.4
local kLoopPeriod = 2.0
local kPatterns = { "asc", "desc", "center", "random" }

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local loopedTime = ctx.time % kLoopPeriod
    local patternIndex = math.floor(ctx.time / kLoopPeriod) % #kPatterns + 1
    local pattern = kPatterns[patternIndex]

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local progress
        if pattern == "asc" then
            progress = mt.stagger(loopedTime, index, kDelay, kDuration)
        else
            progress = mt.stagger_pattern(
                loopedTime,
                index,
                ctx.char_count,
                pattern,
                kDelay,
                kDuration,
                ctx.meta.instance_seed
            )
        end
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - mt.ease.out_cubic(progress)) * 0.15
    end
end
description:
Create per-character delays with mt.stagger, then compare ascending, descending,
center-out, and random ordering with mt.stagger_pattern.
title: MT Stagger
author: Mug

name: 15_mt_random_noise.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title MT Random Noise
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Use deterministic random values for stable variation and noise for smooth
time-varying motion. Both are safe during scrubbing and parallel rendering.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do

        -- Named channels produce independent values from the same seed and index.
        local stableScale = mt.random(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, "scale")
        local stableRotation =
            mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, -8.0, 8.0, "rotation")
        character.scale = 0.85 + stableScale * 0.3
        character.rotation = stableRotation

        -- Move the sample position with time for continuous motion.
        local oneDimensionalNoise =
            mt.noise1(ctx.time * 1.5 + index * 0.4, ctx.meta.instance_seed)
        local twoDimensionalNoise =
            mt.noise2(ctx.time, index * 0.3, ctx.meta.instance_seed + 2)
        character.offset_x =
            0.5 + oneDimensionalNoise * character.geometry.advance_x * 0.2
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + twoDimensionalNoise * 0.03
    end
end
description:
Use deterministic random values for stable variation and noise for smooth
time-varying motion. Both are safe during scrubbing and parallel rendering.
title: MT Random Noise
author: Mug

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ123"
-- @title MT Easing
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Compare every easing curve with the same 0–1 input. Each character uses the
corresponding function in the table below.
]]

local kEasingFunctions = {
    mt.ease.linear,
    mt.ease.in_quad, mt.ease.out_quad, mt.ease.in_out_quad,
    mt.ease.in_cubic, mt.ease.out_cubic, mt.ease.in_out_cubic,
    mt.ease.in_quart, mt.ease.out_quart, mt.ease.in_out_quart,
    mt.ease.in_sine, mt.ease.out_sine, mt.ease.in_out_sine,
    mt.ease.in_circ, mt.ease.out_circ, mt.ease.in_out_circ,
    mt.ease.in_expo, mt.ease.out_expo, mt.ease.in_out_expo,
    mt.ease.in_back, mt.ease.out_back, mt.ease.in_out_back,
    mt.ease.in_elastic, mt.ease.out_elastic, mt.ease.in_out_elastic,
    mt.ease.in_bounce, mt.ease.out_bounce, mt.ease.in_out_bounce,
    function(progress)
        return mt.ease.cubic_bezier(0.42, 0.0, 0.58, 1.0, progress)
    end,
}

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local progress = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 2.0)
    for index, evaluate in ipairs(kEasingFunctions) do
        if index <= ctx.char_count then
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.offset_y = 0.4 + evaluate(progress) * 0.2
        end
    end
end
description:
Compare every easing curve with the same 0–1 input. Each character uses the
corresponding function in the table below.
title: MT Easing
author: Mug

name: 18_mt_keyframes.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @title MT Keyframes
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Build a multi-pose animation with mt.keyframes. Numeric and color values are
interpolated directly from the current time without stored state.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 1 then
        return
    end

    -- Numeric keyframes: fall in with a bounce, hold, then ease out.
    -- Looped over a repeating window so the whole sequence replays.
    local loopedTime = ctx.time % 2.0
    local keyframedOffset = mt.keyframes({
        { t = 0.0, v = -0.15 },
        { t = 0.3, v = 0.0, ease = "out_bounce" },
        { t = 1.2, v = 0.0 },
        { t = 1.6, v = -0.15, ease = "in_cubic" },
    }, loopedTime)
    ctx.chars[1].offset_y = 0.5 + keyframedOffset

    -- Color keyframes: the same function interpolates { r, g, b, a } tables
    -- directly -- no separate color-specific keyframe helper needed. A
    -- single `keys` array must be all-number or all-color, never mixed.
    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        local tint = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 } },
            { t = 1.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 0.4, b = 0.1, a = 1.0 }, ease = "out_cubic" },
            { t = 2.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_cubic" },
        }, loopedTime)
        ctx.chars[2].fill.use = true
        ctx.chars[2].fill.color = tint
    end
end
description:
Build a multi-pose animation with mt.keyframes. Numeric and color values are
interpolated directly from the current time without stored state.
title: MT Keyframes
author: Mug

name: 19_mt_layout_reflow.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @title MT Layout Reflow
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Restore spacing and baseline alignment after per-character scale or stretch.
Call mt.layout.reflow as the final layout operation for the frame.
]]

local kAnchorIndex = 1

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kAnchorIndex then
        return
    end

    -- reflow preserves the anchor's current transformed typesetting origin.
    -- Put its scale pivot on the horizontal baseline so the anchor itself
    -- cannot move the whole line vertically while its scale changes.
    local anchor = ctx.chars[kAnchorIndex]
    anchor.pivot_y = 0.5
        + anchor.geometry.canvas_origin_y
        - anchor.geometry.bounds_center_y

    -- Pass 1: any per-character size animation. Left alone, scaling around
    -- each character's own natural center would drift the baseline and
    -- crowd/gap the neighbors.
    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        character.scale = 0.6 + 0.4 * mt.stagger(ctx.time % 2.0, index, 0.1, 0.5)
    end

    -- Pass 2: re-typeset the whole line using scaled font advances and a
    -- small extra gap (as a fraction of canvas width). This does not
    -- equalize the visible ink gap between unlike glyph shapes.
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.01, { anchor = kAnchorIndex })
end
description:
Restore spacing and baseline alignment after per-character scale or stretch.
Call mt.layout.reflow as the final layout operation for the frame.
title: MT Layout Reflow
author: Mug

name: 20_mt_layout_reflow_options.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "ABCDEFGH"
-- @title MT Layout Reflow Comparison
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Compare partial scaling without reflow against corrected spacing. Red characters
shrink, separate, reflow, overlap while growing, then reflow again.
]]

local kTargetIndices = { 3, 4, 5, 6 }
local kAnchorIndex = 3
local kShrunkScale = 0.55
local kFullScale = 1.0

local kHoldFullEnd = 0.5
local kShrinkEnd = 1.5
local kHoldShrunkEnd = 2.0
local kAlignShrunkEnd = 2.5
local kGrowOverlapEnd = 3.5
local kHoldOverlapEnd = 4.0
local kAlignFullEnd = 4.5

local function applyScale(ctx, scale)
    for _, index in ipairs(kTargetIndices) do
        if index <= ctx.char_count then
            ctx.chars[index].scale = scale
        end
    end
end

-- Reflow at one scale, then restore another scale for display. This makes
-- the overlap caused by growing beyond the packed layout easy to see.
local function reflowAtScale(ctx, layoutScale, displayScale)
    applyScale(ctx, layoutScale)
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
        targets = kTargetIndices,
        anchor = kAnchorIndex,
    })
    applyScale(ctx, displayScale)
end

local function colorCharacters(ctx)
    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local isTarget =
            index >= kTargetIndices[1]
            and index <= kTargetIndices[#kTargetIndices]
        character.fill.use = true
        if isTarget then
            character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.35, b = 0.35, a = 1.0 }
        else
            character.fill.color = { r = 0.6, g = 0.6, b = 0.6, a = 1.0 }
        end
    end
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    colorCharacters(ctx)

    if ctx.time < kHoldFullEnd then
        applyScale(ctx, kFullScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kShrinkEnd then
        local progress = mt.smoothstep(kHoldFullEnd, kShrinkEnd, ctx.time)
        applyScale(ctx, mt.lerp(kFullScale, kShrunkScale, progress))
    elseif ctx.time < kHoldShrunkEnd then
        -- No reflow: each character shrinks around its own center, leaving gaps.
        applyScale(ctx, kShrunkScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kAlignShrunkEnd then
        -- Reflow closes the gaps while character 3 remains anchored.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, kShrunkScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kGrowOverlapEnd then
        local progress = mt.smoothstep(kAlignShrunkEnd, kGrowOverlapEnd, ctx.time)
        local displayScale = mt.lerp(kShrunkScale, kFullScale, progress)
        -- Keep the packed positions while growing to reveal the overlap.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, displayScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kHoldOverlapEnd then
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, kFullScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kAlignFullEnd then
        -- Reflow at full scale resolves the overlap.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kFullScale, kFullScale)
    else
        -- Reflow must run every frame; layout changes are not persistent.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kFullScale, kFullScale)
    end
end
description:
Compare partial scaling without reflow against corrected spacing. Red characters
shrink, separate, reflow, overlap while growing, then reflow again.
title: MT Layout Reflow Comparison
author: Mug

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @recommend text "AB"
-- @title MT Path
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Build point-to-point Bezier motion and waypoint-based Catmull–Rom motion.
Both helpers return coordinates for the current 0–1 progress.
]]

local kBezierPoints = {
    { x = 0.25, y = 0.35 },
    { x = 0.25, y = 0.75 },
    { x = 0.75, y = 0.75 },
    { x = 0.75, y = 0.35 },
}

local kCatmullRomPoints = {
    { x = 0.2, y = 0.3 },
    { x = 0.35, y = 0.65 },
    { x = 0.65, y = 0.35 },
    { x = 0.8, y = 0.7 },
}

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local progress = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 2.0)

    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        local x, y = mt.path.bezier(
            kBezierPoints[1],
            kBezierPoints[2],
            kBezierPoints[3],
            kBezierPoints[4],
            progress
        )
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, ctx.chars[1], x, y)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        local x, y = mt.path.catmull_rom(kCatmullRomPoints, progress)
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, ctx.chars[2], x, y)
    end
end
description:
Build point-to-point Bezier motion and waypoint-based Catmull–Rom motion.
Both helpers return coordinates for the current 0–1 progress.
title: MT Path

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @title MT Text
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Extract text by character index with mt.text.slice. Unlike string.sub, it is
safe for accented text, Japanese, and emoji.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- 1-based, inclusive character range; endChar defaults to the end of
    -- the string when omitted.
    print("slice(text, 1, 3) =", mt.text.slice(ctx.global.text, 1, 3))
    print("slice(text, 2) =", mt.text.slice(ctx.global.text, 2))
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Practical use: highlight the first half of the text differently from
    -- the second half, splitting on a CHARACTER boundary rather than a byte
    -- boundary (safe even if the text contains multibyte characters).
    local halfLength = math.floor(ctx.char_count / 2)

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        character.fill.use = true
        if index <= halfLength then
            character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.6, b = 0.2, a = 1.0 }
        else
            character.fill.color = { r = 0.2, g = 0.6, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
        end
    end
end
description:
Extract text by character index with mt.text.slice. Unlike string.sub, it is
safe for accented text, Japanese, and emoji.
title: MT Text

name: 23_mt_aspect_ratio.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "OOOOOOOO++++++++"
-- @title MT Aspect Ratio Correction
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Compare an uncorrected normalized circle with an aspect-corrected circle.
Only the corrected path keeps a constant physical radius.
]]

local kMarkersPerCircle = 8
local kRadius = 0.12
local kRawCenterX = 0.28
local kCorrectedCenterX = 0.72
local kCenterY = 0.5

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local rotation = mt.friction_decay(ctx.time, 90.0, 0.8)

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local groupIndex = math.floor((index - 1) / kMarkersPerCircle) + 1
        local markerIndex = (index - 1) % kMarkersPerCircle + 1
        local isCorrected = groupIndex == 2
        local centerX = isCorrected and kCorrectedCenterX or kRawCenterX
        local angle =
            mt.distribute(markerIndex, kMarkersPerCircle) * 360.0 + rotation
        local offsetX, offsetY = mt.polar_offset_2d(angle, kRadius)

        -- Equal normalized X/Y offsets form a wide ellipse on a wide canvas.
        -- Dividing X by width/height restores equal physical radii.
        local correctedOffsetX =
            isCorrected and offsetX / ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio or offsetX
        local targetX = centerX + correctedOffsetX
        local targetY = kCenterY + offsetY

        local physicalRadius =
            mt.layout.radial_distance(ctx, targetX, targetY, centerX, kCenterY)
        local radiusAccuracy =
            mt.falloff(math.abs(physicalRadius - kRadius), 0.025)

        character.scale = 0.35 + radiusAccuracy * 0.25
        character.opacity = 0.35 + radiusAccuracy * 0.65
        character.fill.use = true
        if isCorrected then
            character.fill.color = { r = 0.1, g = 0.75, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
        else
            character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.35, b = 0.1, a = 1.0 }
        end
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, targetX, targetY)
    end
end
description:
Compare an uncorrected normalized circle with an aspect-corrected circle.
Only the corrected path keeps a constant physical radius.
title: MT Aspect Ratio Correction
author: Mug

name: 24_mt_layout_position.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "ABC"
-- @title MT Layout Position
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Place characters and parts at exact canvas positions through transformed
hierarchies. Shows the calculation API and its mutating convenience wrapper.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- A non-identity parent transform makes direct offset assignment incorrect.
    ctx.global.rotation = 12.0
    ctx.global.scale = 0.9
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local phase = ctx.time * 1.5
    local targetX = 0.5 + math.cos(phase) * 0.18
    local targetY = 0.5 + math.sin(phase) * 0.12

    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[1]
        -- Calculate offsets without mutation, then apply both components.
        local offsetX, offsetY =
            mt.layout.canvas_to_offset_2d(ctx, character, targetX, targetY)
        character.offset_x = offsetX
        character.offset_y = offsetY

        local actualX, actualY = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, character)
        character.opacity = 1.0 - math.min(math.abs(actualX - targetX) + math.abs(actualY - targetY), 1.0)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        -- place_2d performs the same calculation and writes the offsets.
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, ctx.chars[2], 1.0 - targetX, targetY)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 3 and ctx.chars[3].part_count > 0 then
        -- The same API handles a part through its owning-character hierarchy.
        local part = ctx.parts[ctx.chars[3].part_start]
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, part, 0.5, 1.0 - targetY)
    end
end
description:
Place characters and parts at exact canvas positions through transformed
hierarchies. Shows the calculation API and its mutating convenience wrapper.
title: MT Layout Position
author: Mug

name: 25_mt_layout_bounds.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "MW+++++"
-- @title MT Layout Bounds
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Measure transformed 2D bounds. Four orange markers follow the corners, while
the yellow marker follows the center.
]]

local kCharacterTargets = { 1, 2 }
local kFirstMarkerIndex = 3
local kMarkerCount = 5
local kComparisonTolerance = 0.000001
local kCycleSeconds = 5.0

local function assertClose(actual, expected, message)
    assert(math.abs(actual - expected) <= kComparisonTolerance, message)
end

local function collectOwnedParts(ctx)
    local targets = {}
    for partIndex, part in mt.each_part(ctx) do
        if part.character_index == 1 or part.character_index == 2 then
            table.insert(targets, partIndex)
        end
    end
    return targets
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local angle = ctx.time / kCycleSeconds * math.pi * 2.0
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.position_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.rotation = 8.0 * math.sin(angle)
    ctx.global.scale = 0.9
    ctx.global.stretch_x = 1.05
    ctx.global.stretch_y = 0.95
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kFirstMarkerIndex + kMarkerCount - 1 then
        return
    end

    local angle = ctx.time / kCycleSeconds * math.pi * 2.0
    local firstCharacter = ctx.chars[1]
    local secondCharacter = ctx.chars[2]

    firstCharacter.scale = 1.15 + 0.25 * math.sin(angle)
    firstCharacter.stretch_x = 1.2
    firstCharacter.stretch_y = 0.8
    firstCharacter.rotation = 28.0 * math.sin(angle)
    firstCharacter.pivot_x = 0.58
    firstCharacter.pivot_y = 0.43

    secondCharacter.scale = 1.0 + 0.2 * math.cos(angle)
    secondCharacter.stretch_x = 0.75
    secondCharacter.stretch_y = 1.25
    secondCharacter.rotation = -34.0 * math.cos(angle)
    secondCharacter.pivot_x = 0.42
    secondCharacter.pivot_y = 0.57

    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, firstCharacter, 0.4, 0.52)
    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, secondCharacter, 0.6, 0.48)

    firstCharacter.fill.use = true
    firstCharacter.fill.color = { r = 0.15, g = 0.55, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    secondCharacter.fill.use = true
    secondCharacter.fill.color = { r = 0.15, g = 0.8, b = 0.95, a = 1.0 }

    -- Omitting targetType selects character indices.
    local characterBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, kCharacterTargets)
    assert(characterBounds ~= nil, "character bounds must be measurable")

    -- The explicit "part" form accepts global part indices.
    local partTargets = collectOwnedParts(ctx)
    local partBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, partTargets, "part")
    assert(partBounds ~= nil, "part bounds must be measurable")
    assertClose(partBounds.left, characterBounds.left, "part/character left mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.right, characterBounds.right, "part/character right mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.bottom, characterBounds.bottom, "part/character bottom mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.top, characterBounds.top, "part/character top mismatch")

    local markerPositions = {
        { x = characterBounds.left, y = characterBounds.top },
        { x = characterBounds.right, y = characterBounds.top },
        { x = characterBounds.right, y = characterBounds.bottom },
        { x = characterBounds.left, y = characterBounds.bottom },
        { x = characterBounds.center_x, y = characterBounds.center_y },
    }

    for markerOffset, position in ipairs(markerPositions) do
        local marker = ctx.chars[kFirstMarkerIndex + markerOffset - 1]
        local isCenterMarker = markerOffset == kMarkerCount
        marker.scale = isCenterMarker and 0.32 or 0.24
        marker.fill.use = true
        if isCenterMarker then
            marker.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.92, b = 0.15, a = 1.0 }
        else
            marker.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.35, b = 0.08, a = 1.0 }
        end
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, marker, position.x, position.y)
    end
end
description:
Measure transformed 2D bounds. Four orange markers follow the corners, while
the yellow marker follows the center.
title: MT Layout Bounds
author: Mug

-- @title MT Path Queue Configurations
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Compare path queues moving left-to-right, right-to-left, and vertically.
Each two-second phase shows the required targets, mode, and heading correction.
]]

local kConfigurations = {
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.1, y = 0.45 }, { x = 0.35, y = 0.62 },
            { x = 0.65, y = 0.38 }, { x = 0.9, y = 0.55 },
        },
        reverseTargets = false,
        mode = "horizontal",
        headingCorrection = 0.0,
    },
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.9, y = 0.45 }, { x = 0.65, y = 0.62 },
            { x = 0.35, y = 0.38 }, { x = 0.1, y = 0.55 },
        },
        reverseTargets = true,
        mode = "horizontal",
        headingCorrection = 180.0,
    },
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.15 }, { x = 0.65, y = 0.35 },
            { x = 0.35, y = 0.65 }, { x = 0.5, y = 0.85 },
        },
        reverseTargets = true,
        mode = "vertical",
        headingCorrection = 90.0,
    },
}

local function configurationIndex(time)
    return math.floor(time / 2.0) % #kConfigurations + 1
end

local function orderedTargets(characterCount, reverse)
    local targets = {}
    for offset = 1, characterCount do
        local index = reverse and (characterCount - offset + 1) or offset
        targets[#targets + 1] = index
    end
    return targets
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local configuration = kConfigurations[configurationIndex(ctx.time)]
    ctx.global.vertical = configuration.mode == "vertical"
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local configuration = kConfigurations[configurationIndex(ctx.time)]
    local phaseTime = ctx.time % 2.0
    local path = mt.path.arc_length(configuration.points, ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio)
    local pathLength = path:length()
    local slots = mt.layout.queue_on_path(ctx, path, {
        align = "end",
        gap = math.min(0.004, pathLength * 0.01),
        mode = configuration.mode,
        targets = orderedTargets(ctx.char_count, configuration.reverseTargets),
    })
    local sharedProgress = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(phaseTime / 1.5))

    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local distanceRatio = math.min(sharedProgress, slots[index])
        local x, y, heading = path:at_distance(distanceRatio)
        character.rotation = heading + configuration.headingCorrection
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, x, y)
    end
end
description:
Compare path queues moving left-to-right, right-to-left, and vertically.
Each two-second phase shows the required targets, mode, and heading correction.
title: MT Path Queue Configurations
author: Mug

--[[ @description
Compare projectile configurations with different launch angles, gravity,
drag, and spin. The motion restarts every three seconds.
]]

local kLaunches = {
    { speed = 0.35, angle = -70.0, gravity = 0.35, drag = 0.0, spin = 45.0 },
    { speed = 0.35, angle = -90.0, gravity = 0.35, drag = 0.8, spin = 0.0 },
    { speed = 0.35, angle = -110.0, gravity = 0.6, drag = 0.2, spin = -45.0 },

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local elapsed = ctx.time % 3.0
    for index, launch in ipairs(kLaunches) do
        if index <= ctx.char_count then
            local result = mt.projectile_2d({
                t = elapsed,
                speed = launch.speed,
                angle = launch.angle,
                gravity = launch.gravity,
                drag = launch.drag,
                spin = launch.spin,
            })
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.offset_x = 0.5 + result.x
            character.offset_y = 0.5 + result.y
            character.rotation = result.rotation
        end

end

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- @recommend text "ABCDE"
-- @title MT Bounce
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Compare ground and wall convenience APIs with the low-level X/Y solvers and
a standalone impact squash. Parameters are grouped by collision type.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local elapsed = ctx.time % 3.0

    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        mt.bounce_ground(ctx, ctx.chars[1], 0.32, {
            t = elapsed,
            start_mode = "absolute",
            start_y = 0.75,
            ground_mode = "absolute",
            gravity = 0.8,
            restitution = 0.55,
            squash = 0.18,
        })
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        mt.bounce_wall(ctx, ctx.chars[2], 0.72, {
            t = elapsed,
            start_mode = "absolute",
            start_x = 0.25,
            wall_mode = "absolute",
            acceleration = 0.8,
            restitution = 0.5,
            squash = 0.18,
        })
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 3 then
        local bounce = mt.bounce_y({
            t = elapsed,
            ground_y = 0.35,
            start_y = 0.75,
            gravity = 0.8,
            restitution = 0.5,
        })
        local character = ctx.chars[3]
        character.stretch_x = bounce.stretch_x
        character.stretch_y = bounce.stretch_y
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, 0.45, bounce.y)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 4 then
        local bounce = mt.bounce_x({
            t = elapsed,
            wall_x = 0.72,
            start_x = 0.25,
            acceleration = 0.8,
            restitution = 0.5,
        })
        local character = ctx.chars[4]
        character.stretch_x = bounce.stretch_x
        character.stretch_y = bounce.stretch_y
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, bounce.x, 0.55)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 5 then
        local impactTime = math.floor(ctx.time) + 0.25
        local stretchX, stretchY, offsetCorrection = mt.impact_squash({
            t = ctx.time,
            impact_time = impactTime,
            squash = 0.25,
            stiffness = 22.0,
            damping = 10.0,
        })
        local character = ctx.chars[5]
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + offsetCorrection * character.geometry.bounds_height
    end
end
description:
Compare ground and wall convenience APIs with the low-level X/Y solvers and
a standalone impact squash. Parameters are grouped by collision type.
title: MT Bounce
author: Mug

name: 29_mt_timeline_chain.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- @recommend text "A"
-- @title MT Timeline Chain
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 4
--[[ @description
Chain a Bezier entrance, hold, bounce, flexible idle, and outro. Each evaluator
receives the prior segment's final value, while remaining keeps the outro
anchored to the clip tail.
]]

local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kEnterDuration = 1.0
local kLandingHoldDuration = 0.25
local kBounceDuration = 1.4
local kOutroDuration = 0.6

local kEnterPath = {
    { x = 0.12, y = 0.25 },
    { x = 0.2, y = 0.85 },
    { x = 0.65, y = 0.9 },
    { x = 0.72, y = 0.7 },
}

local kInitialState = {
    x = kEnterPath[1].x,
    y = kEnterPath[1].y,
    stretch_x = 1.0,
    stretch_y = 1.0,
    opacity = 0.0,
}

local function evaluateEnter(segmentCtx, previous)
    local progress = mt.ease.out_cubic(segmentCtx.timeline.progress)
    local positionX, positionY =
        mt.path.bezier(kEnterPath[1], kEnterPath[2], kEnterPath[3], kEnterPath[4], progress)
    return {
        x = positionX,
        y = positionY,
        stretch_x = previous.stretch_x,
        stretch_y = previous.stretch_y,
        opacity = progress,
    }
end

local function evaluateBounce(segmentCtx, previous)
    local bounce = mt.bounce_y({
        t = segmentCtx.time,
        ground_y = 0.35,
        start_y = previous.y,
        gravity = 1.6,
        restitution = 0.48,
        squash = 0.2,
    })
    return {
        x = previous.x,
        y = bounce.y,
        stretch_x = bounce.stretch_x,
        stretch_y = bounce.stretch_y,
        opacity = previous.opacity,
    }
end

local function evaluateIdle(segmentCtx, previous)
    return {
        x = previous.x + math.sin(segmentCtx.time * 1.7) * 0.015,
        y = previous.y + math.sin(segmentCtx.time * 2.3) * 0.012,
        stretch_x = previous.stretch_x,
        stretch_y = previous.stretch_y,
        opacity = previous.opacity,
    }
end

local function evaluateOutro(segmentCtx, previous)
    local progress = mt.ease.in_cubic(segmentCtx.timeline.progress)
    return {
        x = previous.x + progress * 0.25,
        y = previous.y + progress * 0.35,
        stretch_x = mt.lerp(previous.stretch_x, 0.75, progress),
        stretch_y = mt.lerp(previous.stretch_y, 1.3, progress),
        opacity = previous.opacity * (1.0 - progress),
    }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 1 then
        return
    end

    local state = mt.timeline.chain(ctx, kInitialState, {
        { duration = kEnterDuration, evaluate = evaluateEnter },
        { hold = kLandingHoldDuration },
        { duration = kBounceDuration, evaluate = evaluateBounce },
        { duration = "remaining", evaluate = evaluateIdle },
        { duration = kOutroDuration, evaluate = evaluateOutro },
    }, {
        fallback_duration = kFallbackClipLength,
    })

    local character = ctx.chars[1]
    character.stretch_x = state.stretch_x
    character.stretch_y = state.stretch_y
    character.opacity = state.opacity
    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, state.x, state.y)
end
description:
Chain a Bezier entrance, hold, bounce, flexible idle, and outro. Each evaluator
receives the prior segment's final value, while remaining keeps the outro
anchored to the clip tail.
title: MT Timeline Chain
author: Mug

name: 30_mt_layout_group_by_line.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend pos 0.5 0.85
-- @recommend text "花鳥風月\n山紫水明"
-- @title MT Layout Group By Line
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 6
--[[ @description
Slide in each vertical column, then reveal its characters from top to bottom.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local columns = mt.layout.group_by_line(ctx)
    for columnOrder, column in ipairs(columns) do
        local columnStart = (columnOrder - 1) * 0.8
        local columnProgress =
            mt.timeline.window_progress(ctx, columnStart, 0.7)
        local columnEase = mt.ease.out_back(columnProgress)
        local columnOffsetX = mt.lerp(0.18, 0.0, columnEase)

        for indexInColumn, character in ipairs(column.items) do
            local characterStart = columnStart + 0.15 + (indexInColumn - 1) * 0.12
            local characterProgress =
                mt.timeline.window_progress(ctx, characterStart, 0.45)
            local characterEase = mt.ease.out_cubic(characterProgress)

            character.offset_x = 0.5 + columnOffsetX
            character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.lerp(-0.04, 0.0, characterEase)
            character.scale = mt.lerp(0.7, 1.0, characterEase)
            character.opacity = characterEase
        end
    end
end
description: Slide in each vertical column, then reveal its characters from top to bottom.
title: MT Layout Group By Line
author: Mug

--[[ @description

normalized progress for opacity.

function OnLayout(ctx)
    for index, character in mt.each_char(ctx) do
        local characterCtx = mt.timeline.window_ctx(ctx, (index - 1) * 0.12, 1.4)

        mt.bounce_ground(characterCtx, character, 0.3, {
            start_mode = "relative",
            ground_mode = "relative",
            align_to = "baseline",
            drop_height = 0.25,
            gravity = 2.5,
            restitution = 0.45,
            squash = 0.12,
        })

        character.opacity = mt.ease.out_cubic(characterCtx.timeline.progress)
    end
end

    "bottom_right",

}

--[[ @description
A rocket flies left to right across the text. Characters stay hidden until
the rocket passes their position, then fade in.

-- Adapted from Google Material Icons "rocket_launch" (Apache License 2.0).
-- Source: https://github.com/google/material-design-icons
local rocketIcon = mt.svg_path([[
M9.19,6.35

s0.7-4.94,1.88-6.12
C4.42,15.34,5.17,15,6,15
C7.66,15,9,16.34,9,18
M13,9
c0-1.1,0.9-2,2-2
s2,0.9,2,2
s-0.9,2-2,2
S13,10.1,13,9
Z
]], {
    view_box = { 0, 0, 24, 24 },
    em_scale = 1.6,
})

local kRocketCharacter = "□"
local kFlightStartCanvasX = -0.15
local kFlightEndCanvasX = 1.15
local kFlightSeconds = 3.0
local kRocketRotationDegrees = 45.0
local kFadeInSpanCanvasWidths = 0.08

local cachedRocketCharacterIndex = 0

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.h_align = "left"
    ctx.global.text = ctx.global.text .. kRocketCharacter
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    cachedRocketCharacterIndex = ctx.char_count

    local characterCanvasX = {}
    for index = 1, cachedRocketCharacterIndex - 1 do
        characterCanvasX[index] = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, ctx.chars[index])
    end

    local flightProgress = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(ctx.time / kFlightSeconds))
    local rocketCanvasX = mt.lerp(kFlightStartCanvasX, kFlightEndCanvasX, flightProgress)

    local rocketCharacter = ctx.chars[cachedRocketCharacterIndex]
    local _, rocketCanvasY = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, rocketCharacter)
    rocketCharacter.offset_x, rocketCharacter.offset_y =
        mt.layout.canvas_to_offset_2d(ctx, rocketCharacter, rocketCanvasX, rocketCanvasY)
    rocketCharacter.rotation = kRocketRotationDegrees

    for index = 1, cachedRocketCharacterIndex - 1 do
        local passedDistance = rocketCanvasX - characterCanvasX[index]
        ctx.chars[index].opacity = mt.saturate(passedDistance / kFadeInSpanCanvasWidths)
    end
end

function OnPath(ctx)
    for _, part in ipairs(ctx.paths:character(cachedRocketCharacterIndex)) do
        part.path:assign(rocketIcon)
    end
end
description:
A rocket flies left to right across the text. Characters stay hidden until
the rocket passes their position, then fade in.
title: Custom SVG Path
